metadata.title: Elon Musk Tesla pay ratio hit 2.5 million to 1 in 2025

content.text:
Elon Musk's $158 billion compensation package at Tesla was 2,522,203 times the median Tesla employee's pay in 2025, according to the AFL-CIO's annual executive paywatch report. The labor federation said the package was 14 times larger than the combined total compensation of all other S&P 500 CEOs.
Musk's pay inflated the average compensation figure for S&P 500 CEOs to $340.1 million in 2025, a roughly 1,700% increase over the prior year. Excluding Musk, average CEO pay at S&P 500 companies rose 21%, from $18.9 million in 2024 to $22.8 million in 2025 — the highest figure since the AFL-CIO began tracking compensation in the 1990s, according to Forbes. Fred Redmond, the AFL-CIO's secretary-treasurer, said in comments reported by Forbes that Musk's Tesla arrangement "changes the dynamic when other CEO compensation plans come up" and that "boards use it as a reference."
Including Musk, the average CEO-to-worker pay ratio across S&P 500 companies reached 5,387-to-1 in 2025. Excluding him, the ratio was 312-to-1, up from 285-to-1 in 2024, the AFL-CIO said. Manufacturing was the highest-paying sector, with an average CEO-to-worker pay ratio of 11,139-to-1, driven by Musk's Tesla package.
Musk's total compensation is based on the grant-date fair value of restricted Tesla stock awarded to him in 2025. Those awards could ultimately be worth up to $1 trillion if Tesla meets various performance targets, the AFL-CIO said. Tesla shareholders approved the compensation package, which includes goals such as the company's market valuation topping $8.5 trillion within 10 years.
Musk's compensation alone surpassed what Tesla took in from customers across all of 2025 — $94 billion in total revenue that itself represented a 3% drop from the prior year, the first time in the company's history that annual revenue had shrunk, according to Electrek. On the bottom line, Tesla's GAAP earnings shrank by 61% year over year in 2025, Electrek also noted. Tesla reported owing $0 in U.S. federal income taxes on $5.68 billion in adjusted income that year, the AFL-CIO said.
Tesla's finances have since shown a partial rebound. The company posted second-quarter 2026 revenue of $28.24 billion, up 26% year over year, crossing $100 billion in trailing twelve-month revenue for the first time. However, GAAP net income dropped 5% from a year earlier to $1.11 billion, and the company reported a free cash flow deficit of $1.09 billion in the quarter.
The AFL-CIO report also noted that in 2025, the median Tesla employee earned $57,243 — meaning Musk received the equivalent of one median worker's annual pay every 4.23 seconds.
